implementerProof.how: Three of the four proof entries reproduced exactly; the fourth carries a claim the artefact it cites contradicts, which is the failure below. (1) The image half: a Job of my own on the round's image, ghcr.io/sjawhar/legion-worker:sha-afa29128061f, gave the same five paths and versions (psql (PostgreSQL) 17.11, redis-cli 8.0.2, sqlite3 3.46.1, OpenBSD netcat 1.229-1, DiG 9.20.30-1~deb13u1-Debian), and that image's own `legion probe-image` printed the 16-name toolchain row and its OK line. (2) The runner half reproduced in this live role container, with the documented form printing Version: 2.6.3. (3) The round's new coordinate control reproduced exactly: `bunx biome@0.3.3 --version` prints 0.3.3 and exits 0 — the version pin obeyed to the letter, still the squatter — and `npm view` answers the two blocks the documents quote, the squatter with no repository.url and no homepage, @biomejs/biome with git+https://github.com/biomejs/biome.git and https://biomejs.dev. (4) The cost entry: head :sha-afa29128061f 24 layers / 1,076,764,060 bytes, base :sha-92dbeea3d391 24 layers / 1,068,477,764 bytes, delta 8,286,296 bytes, the runtime Debian layer 327,156,512 -> 335,441,703 = 8,285,191 bytes, and the two revisions afa29128061fc10dd6c6aa3755ba051b98b84e02 and 92dbeea3d3911b5fb08e279fb201634a84ffe72e read from the config blobs — every one of those reproduced from the same manifests. Its last clause, 'every other layer is within 2 KB of compression noise', does not: two layers differ by more than 2 KB. That clause is shipped in docs/kubernetes.md as well, which is why this is a failure rather than a note.

failures.criterion: The choice is written down with the measurement that decided it, so the next reader is not left to infer the cost.
failures.evidence: docs/kubernetes.md, 'Image size and pull time': '… 8,286,296 bytes, of which the runtime stage's Debian layer is 8,285,191 bytes (327,156,512 → 335,441,703) and every other layer differs by at most 2 KB' (the same claim in .legion/INFRA-221/implement.json proof[3] as 'every other layer is within 2 KB of compression noise'). Measured from the two manifests that sentence cites, read with a GHCR pull token and compared layer by layer by position (ghcr.io/v2/sjawhar/legion-worker/manifests/sha-afa29128061f and .../sha-92dbeea3d391, 24 layers each): two non-Debian layers differ by more than 2 KB — layer 8, 226,140 → 228,880 bytes (+2,740), and layer 11, 120,624,977 → 120,621,813 bytes (−3,164). The true bounds are 3,164 bytes for the largest single layer and 1,105 bytes net across all 23 non-Debian layers (8,286,296 − 8,285,191). Every other figure in that paragraph reproduced exactly, so the correction is the one clause, in docs/kubernetes.md and in the handoff: for example 'every other layer differs by at most 3,164 bytes, 1,105 bytes net'. No red test accompanies this one: the repository's testing rules forbid a test over documentation prose, and a permanent test that reads two GHCR manifests at run time would be a network-dependent lock on two build artefacts; the reproduction command above is the check, and it is in this handoff.

proof.criterion: A role that needs a tool its work requires can get it, in one documented step, without a person — the image half, at this round's head, and the build gate the round added for `nc`.
proof.surface: A Job in this role's own cluster namespace (its name read from the projected token file), under the namespace's admission policy (Job deadline, the deployment's compute class, gVisor, no service-account token, >=4 CPU), running the image this round built: ghcr.io/sjawhar/legion-worker:sha-afa29128061f (manifest sha256:d90d6423241565155b35427e5b32e70c213d121af0d7c08c1d32b23e221a7e6e, config revision afa29128061fc10dd6c6aa3755ba051b98b84e02).
proof.command: bash -c 'type -P psql redis-cli sqlite3 nc dig; psql --version; redis-cli --version; sqlite3 --version; nc -h; dig -v; nc="$(command -v nc)"; test "$nc" = /usr/bin/nc; ls -l /usr/bin/nc /etc/alternatives/nc; grep -n "exact coordinate|bunx biome@0.3.3|npm view <name>" /opt/legion/pi-legion/dist/skills/legion-worker/references/tools.md; legion probe-image --plugin-root /opt/legion/pi-legion --envoy-plugin-root /opt/legion/pi-envoy --skip-agent-models'
proof.observed: type -P printed /usr/bin/psql, /usr/bin/redis-cli, /usr/bin/sqlite3, /usr/bin/nc, /usr/bin/dig and exited 0, and each ran (psql (PostgreSQL) 17.11 (Debian 17.11-0+deb13u1), redis-cli 8.0.2, sqlite3 3.46.1, OpenBSD netcat (Debian patchlevel 1.229-1), DiG 9.20.30-1~deb13u1-Debian). The round's new build gate re-run in the published image: `command -v nc` is /usr/bin/nc and the assertion passed, with /usr/bin/nc -> /etc/alternatives/nc -> /bin/nc.openbsd, so the name the gate pins is the alternatives link the Dockerfile comment describes. The round's rewritten rule ships inside the image: /opt/legion/pi-legion/dist/skills/legion-worker/references/tools.md carries '## Always write the exact coordinate and the exact version' at line 62, the `npm view <name> …` instruction at 68 and the `bunx biome@0.3.3` control at 90. `legion probe-image` printed 'capability toolchain: present (on PATH: … /usr/bin/flock, /usr/bin/psql, /usr/bin/redis-cli, /usr/bin/sqlite3, /usr/bin/nc, /usr/bin/dig; go version go1.27.1 linux/amd64)' and 'probe-image: OK … daemon-api-version=35', exit 0. The Job was deleted; the namespace holds none.
proof.negativeControl: The gate's own assertion driven to failure in the same container: with a dummy `nc` first on PATH (/tmp/fake/nc), `command -v nc` resolved to /tmp/fake/nc and `test "$nc" = /usr/bin/nc` exited 1 — so the new line in the build's final step is a check that can fail, not a tautology. Round 1's control stands unchanged for the image half: the digest the deployment pins today resolves none of the five, and its own probe's toolchain row ends at /usr/bin/flock while still printing probe-image: OK.

proof.criterion: That step never resolves something other than what was asked for: the written rule binds the package's identity, not only its version (review round 1, finding 1).
proof.surface: This live role container against npm's registry, through bun and npm — the surface a role types the documented form into.
proof.command: bunx biome --version; bunx biome@0.3.3 --version; bunx --package @biomejs/biome@2.6.3 biome --version; npm view biome version description repository.url homepage; npm view @biomejs/biome version description repository.url homepage
proof.observed: The bare name printed 0.3.3 (exit 0); the version-pinned bare name printed 0.3.3 (exit 0) — the control the first round lacked, and the one that shows a version pin alone does not defend; only the documented `--package @biomejs/biome@2.6.3 biome` form printed Version: 2.6.3. `npm view biome version description repository.url homepage` answered version = '0.3.3' and the environment-variable description with no repository.url and no homepage line at all; `npm view @biomejs/biome …` answered version = '2.6.3', 'Biome is a toolchain for the web: formatter, linter and more', repository.url = 'git+https://github.com/biomejs/biome.git', homepage = 'https://biomejs.dev'. Both blocks are character-for-character what skills/legion-worker/references/tools.md and docs/kubernetes.md now print, so the check a role is told to run before a tool's first use gives the answer the documents promise.
proof.negativeControl: `bunx biome@0.3.3 --version` is the negative control: it obeys 'write the exact version' and still runs the squatter, exit 0, which is why the rule now has two halves. Nothing in the repository refuses either unpinned form, and both documents say so.

proof.criterion: The written reason for each client is true of the code it cites (review round 1, findings 2 and 3): psql's entry point, and the extraction prefix the 'you cannot install a sixth' claim was replaced with.
proof.surface: The repository's own code, read at this head, and an extraction prefix built in this role container from the same 20 Debian packages the apt line installs.
proof.command: packages/dispatch/package.json scripts; grep for ./psql importers under packages/dispatch/e2e/; then: apt-get … --print-uris bind9-dnsutils netcat-openbsd postgresql-client redis-tools sqlite3 | curl each | dpkg-deb -x into /tmp/prefix; LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/tmp/prefix/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu /tmp/prefix/usr/bin/{redis-cli,sqlite3,dig,psql}
proof.observed: The corrected citation is right: `"e2e": "bun run build:web && playwright test --config e2e/playwright.config.ts"` and `"dispatch:local": "bun e2e/local-instance.ts"` in packages/dispatch/package.json, with e2e/psql.ts imported by e2e/seed.ts (whose resetDatabase every spec reaches) and by five spec files directly, while local-instance.ts is what `dispatch:local` runs — exactly what the Dockerfile comment, image.go and tools.md now say, and not what they said in round 1. The extraction claim is right too, reproduced from scratch: 20 packages, 25 MiB extracted, and with LD_LIBRARY_PATH set redis-cli printed 8.0.2, sqlite3 3.46.1 and dig DiG 9.20.30-1~deb13u1-Debian, while /tmp/prefix/usr/bin/psql (a symlink to ../share/postgresql-common/pg_wrapper) failed with "Can't locate PgCommon.pm in @INC … at /tmp/prefix/usr/bin/psql line 22", exit 2 — the Perl search path the documents name, verbatim.
proof.negativeControl: psql from the prefix is itself the control for the extraction row's 'and psql did not': the three clients that run and the one that cannot were produced by the same command on the same prefix, so the asymmetry is measured rather than asserted. (The row's 30 packages / 11 MiB / 105 MiB are a wider resolution than this 20-package set against the image's installed base; the behaviour, which is what the row rests on, is the part reproduced here.)

previousRounds.summary: Four Jobs on ghcr.io/sjawhar/legion-worker:sha-839ab9e81bfe and this role container: the five clients present and doing real work (sqlite3 on a real database, dig resolving and NXDOMAIN, nc opening ghcr.io:443 and refused on a closed port, and psql/redis-cli against a real PostgreSQL 17 and Redis 8 running as sidecars — select version(), CREATE TABLE/INSERT/SELECT, PING/SET/GET/INFO), the shipped licence and alternatives claims (all five copyright files, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES, /usr/bin/nc as the alternatives link, no /usr/share/doc/dnsutils/copyright), probe-image's 16-name toolchain row, and the three pinned runner forms each failing closed. Negative controls: the pinned digest carries none of the five and its own probe still prints OK; psql masked off PATH makes probe-image fail naming psql.
